items.title: Villager News 1.0 Add-On
items.creator: Oreville Studios
items.description:
BREAKING NEWS! Villager News is live in an official Oreville Studios x Element Animation collaboration! Bring your Villagers to life today!
- 2,000+ voiced reactions!
- Reactive dialogue to mobs, blocks, player actions and more!
- Expressive animations & lip sync!
- Player reputation & gossip systems!
- Special characters & unique trades!

faqEntries.heading: Is the Villager News an official collaboration with Element Animation?
faqEntries.content: Yes! The Villager News Add-On is an official collaboration between Oreville Studios and Element Animation, bringing the world, characters and humour of Villager News in-game.

faqEntries.heading: Is Villager News compatible with Actions & Stuff?
faqEntries.content: Yes! Villager News is fully compatible with Actions & Stuff, but can also be enjoyed on its own.

faqEntries.heading: How do I make Villagers react?
faqEntries.content: Just play normally and experiment around them! Villagers can react to player actions, mobs, blocks, trading, damage, world events and much more. Check the Triggers & Reactions Guide if you want to hunt for specific reactions.

faqEntries.heading: How does Player Reputation work?
faqEntries.content: Villagers remember how you treat them. Trading and curing improves your reputation, while hurting or killing Villagers lowers it. Villagers can also gossip about you, spreading your reputation to others.

faqEntries.heading: Where do I find the special Villager News characters?
faqEntries.content: Special Villager News characters can only spawn in Villages located at least 1,000 blocks away from world spawn. Explore further out to find them, with each character offering their own dialogue and unique trades.

faqEntries.heading: Do Baby Villagers have dialogue too?
faqEntries.content: Yes! Baby Villagers have their own reactions and animations.

howToEntries.content: Villager News brings Villagers to life with reactive dialogue, conversations, animations, reputation and plenty of hidden reactions to discover.
Play normally and experiment! Villagers react to mobs, blocks, trading, damage, player actions, world events and much more. Try doing different things around them and see what they have to say.
Explore Villages to find special Villager News characters. One of each can spawn in your world, with their own personality, dialogue and unique trades.
Treat Villagers carefully! They remember how you behave. Trading and curing improves your reputation, while hurting Villagers lowers it, and they may gossip about you with others.
Customise your experience from the Villager News Handbook in-game. Change Villager texture style, chattiness, rare voice lines, subtitles and toggle to the legacy baby villagers whenever you like.
Keep experimenting. Some reactions are much harder to discover than others. Browse the Triggers & Reactions Guide in-game if you want to see everything Villagers can react to.

faqEntries.heading: Can this Add-On be used without Vibrant Visuals?
faqEntries.content: Yes! Dynamic lighting and block lighting will work with graphics set to Fancy or Simple. Colored lighting, however, requires graphics to be set to Vibrant Visuals.

faqEntries.heading: Where can I find Glowshrooms?
faqEntries.content: Glowshrooms can be found deep underground, commonly in the Deepslate layer below Y=0. They generate in patches and only in newly generated chunks since the Add-On was added to the world. Huge Glowshrooms are much rarer, but generate under the same conditions, provided there is enough space for them to grow.

howToEntries.heading: Turn on Vibrant Visuals
howToEntries.content:
On the Main Menu, click Settings > Video.

Under "Graphics, Performance & Layout" set "Mode" to Vibrant Visuals.

If Vibrant Visuals is grayed out or unavailable, your device does not support Vibrant Visuals or colored lighting.

faqEntries.heading: How do I craft the new blocks?
faqEntries.content: The new blocks can be crafted with special crafting tables, like the Workbench. Hold an Oak Log in your hand and interact with it to open a menu, and select what you want to craft!

faqEntries.heading: What other crafting tables are there?
faqEntries.content: Besides the Workbench, you can use the Carving Table, Forge Table, Textile Bench, Glasswork Station, and Floral Station to craft blocks. Each crafting table has tons of unique blocks!

howToEntries.heading: Step 1: Enable Wonder's Building Blocks Add-On
howToEntries.content: Open your world settings and activate Wonder's Building Blocks Add-On under both Resource Packs and Behavior Packs. Make sure it appears in the Active list.

howToEntries.heading: Step 2: Open the Guide Book
howToEntries.content: When you enter your world, you'll receive the Wonder's Building Blocks Guide Book. Place it on the ground and interact with it to open the guide.

howToEntries.heading: Step 3: Craft your first Workbench
howToEntries.content: Use a Crafting Table to craft a Workbench with a Crafting Table, Oak Planks, and Sticks.

howToEntries.heading: Step 4: Craft Custom Blocks
howToEntries.content: Hold any log in your hand and interact with the Workbench. This will open a menu, and you can click any item inside to turn your logs into it!

items.title: Actually Additions
items.creator: A30x1
items.description:
A long-time fan favorite, Use the Atomic Reconstructor and the Empowerer to turn minerals into powerful crystals that allow the creation of useful machines for processing and sorting items, lasers for wireless energy transporting, items and fluids, renewable oil to generate power, and much more.

- Official Bedrock port of Actually Additions Java Mod

faqEntries.heading: How do I get the guidebook back if I lose it?
faqEntries.content: Each player receives the Actually Additions Manual on their first spawn. If you lose it, you can craft another one on a crafting table with 1 Paper and 1 Canola Seeds. It is your main in-game reference for every recipe and mechanic.

faqEntries.heading: What is CF?
faqEntries.content: CF stands for Crystal Flux, the energy system this add-on uses. Machines need CF to run, generators produce it, and Laser Relays move it between machines.

faqEntries.heading: Why isn't my machine working?
faqEntries.content: The most common reason is no energy. Make sure a generator is producing CF and that the machine either stores its own CF or is connected through Energy Laser Relays.

faqEntries.heading: How do I connect Laser Relays?
faqEntries.content: Place the relays near your machines and use the Laser Wrench to link them into a network.

faqEntries.heading: Where do I find Black Quartz?
faqEntries.content: Black Quartz Ore generates underground in the Overworld. It is used to craft the Iron Casing, which is needed to build the Atomic Reconstructor and other machines.

faqEntries.heading: Where do the crystals come from?
faqEntries.content: You create them with the Atomic Reconstructor using the correct Lens and inputs, then upgrade them into Empowered crystals with the Empowerer.

howToEntries.heading: Getting started
howToEntries.content: When you first enter the world, you automatically receive the Actually Additions Manual. If you ever lose it, craft another with 1 Paper and 1 Canola Seeds on a crafting table. Hold it and interact to open it, then navigate by looking at the on-page buttons. The manual has a page for every block and item, and it is your main reference for recipes and mechanics. To close it, press Sneak or click the X button in the top-right corner. Inside the manual there is a settings screen where you can adjust the cursor sensitivity and the interface scale.

howToEntries.heading: Getting energy (Crystal Flux)
howToEntries.content: Everything in this add-on runs on Crystal Flux (CF). To produce it, craft and place a generator such as the Coal Generator (burns coal and other solid fuels), Oil Generator (burns canola oils), Leaf-Eating Generator, Bio Reactor, or Heat Collector (placed next to lava). Machines store their own CF.

howToEntries.heading: Moving energy around
howToEntries.content: To share CF between machines, place Energy Laser Relays next to them and link the relays with the Laser Wrench. There are basic, advanced, and extreme tiers with higher transfer rates. Item and Fluid Laser Relays move items and fluids the same way.

howToEntries.heading: Getting started with machines
howToEntries.content: Craft the Iron Casing using Black Quartz, then use it to build the Atomic Reconstructor, the core machine of the add-on. Give it Crystal Flux from a generator and it fires a beam that converts items placed in front of it into new ones, including the six crystals when you add the matching Lens.

howToEntries.heading: Upgrading crystals
howToEntries.content: Build the Empowerer with Display Stands around it, place the crystal and the catalyst items on the stands, and supply energy to turn a crystal into its Empowered version.

howToEntries.heading: Farming and processing
howToEntries.content: Use the Farmer and Greenhouse Glass to automate crops (Canola, Rice, Flax, Coffee). Use the Crusher and Double Crusher to grind materials, and the Powered Furnace to smelt with CF instead of fuel.

howToEntries.content:
How to install Hidden Bosses

After downloading Hidden Bosses from the Minecraft Marketplace:

1. Create a new world, or select the pencil icon beside an existing world to edit it.
2. Open Behavior Packs, then select My Packs.
3. Choose Hidden Bosses and select Activate.
4. The required resource pack should activate automatically. If it does not, open Resource Packs, select My Packs, and activate Hidden Bosses
5. Start the world and find those Bosses!

The first time you join, you’ll automatically receive the Hidden Bosses Guide.

We recommend making a backup before adding Hidden Bosses to an existing world.

faqEntries.heading: How can you craft the Redstone Plus Guidebook?
faqEntries.content:
You will be automatically given the guidebook first time when you enter the world, but if you've lost it, it is easy to craft.
You need 1 book and 4 redstone dust.
In a crafting bench, place the book in the centre, with a piece of redstone dust in the 4 spots around the book. 
All other crafting recipes can be found within the guidebook.

faqEntries.heading: What is the maximum range of the wireless redstone unit and wireless lamp?
faqEntries.content: There is no defined maximum range. If the chunk is loaded (for example a player is nearby), the wireless signal will be transmitted/received.

faqEntries.heading: Can you swap the direction of the Redstone Tower?
faqEntries.content: Yes, interacting (right clicking) with the Redstone Tower will flip its direction round so the redstone signal can transfer down, instead of the usual up.

items.changelog: - Added "& Recycling" to title, description & guidebook to match marketing images

faqEntries.heading: What items go in each Recycling Bin?
faqEntries.content: Glass Bin takes glass items, Metal Bin takes ores/ingots/tools, Organic Bin takes food and plant items, and Paper Bin takes paper, books, and similar items.

faqEntries.heading: What happens if I try to recycle, uncraft, or crush a valuable or enchanted item?
faqEntries.content: These blocks will ask you to confirm before consuming it, so you don't lose something valuable by accident.

faqEntries.heading: Can I automate these blocks with hoppers?
faqEntries.content: Yes — Recycling Bins, the Incinerator, and the Stone Crusher can all be fed and emptied with hoppers.

faqEntries.heading: Why won't the Uncrafter give my item back?
faqEntries.content: Some items like planks, raw ores, and a few other base resources can't be uncrafted, to prevent item duplication. Damaged items also can't be uncrafted; they need to be at least half durability to be reversed.

faqEntries.heading: My Trash Collector Golem is holding the wrong item — how do I get it back?
faqEntries.content: Sneak and interact with the golem to retrieve whatever it's currently carrying.

howToEntries.heading: How do the Recycling Bins work?
howToEntries.content: Craft a Glass, Metal, Organic, or Paper Recycling Bin and place it down. Interact with a matching item in hand to feed it into the bin. Once it's full, it produces reward items and XP.

howToEntries.heading: How do I build a golem?
howToEntries.content: Golems are built from Trash Bags and Cardboard Boxes, and the shape you build changes what you get. Stack a Trash Bag directly on top of a Cardboard Box to create a Trash Collector Golem, which automatically picks up nearby items and delivers them to your recycling bins. Build the two blocks in a classic golem shape instead (Trash Bag as the head, Cardboard Boxes forming the body and arms) to create a Trash Golem, a combat guardian that fights off hostile mobs near your base.

howToEntries.heading: How do I use the Incinerator?
howToEntries.content: Craft and place the Incinerator, then interact with the top of the block to open its inventory and deposit unwanted items. Send it a redstone pulse to burn everything inside into Ash and a bit of XP.

howToEntries.heading: How do I use the Uncrafter?
howToEntries.content: Hold the item you want to break back down into materials, then interact with the Uncrafter. If the item can be reversed, it will consume it and give you back its original crafting ingredients.

howToEntries.heading: How do I use the Stone Crusher?
howToEntries.content: Hold a stone-type item or block and interact with the Stone Crusher to grind it into Stone Cobble.
